behaviourPage.aStopStopsTheAgent: A stop stops the agent. A correction or an answer goes into what it is doing, or restarts it if its engine can't take words midway. Each agent can choose for itself in its own settings.
behaviourPage.agentsCanNameTheTask: Agents can name the task when they hand work on. With this set, a reviewer moving from one task to the next isn't stopped as if it were one long exchange. Calling the same work by another name doesn't get past the total, and your next message resets both counts.
behaviourPage.agentsStopAfterThisMany: Agents stop after this many replies to each other, so they can't use up your plan on their own. Your next message resets the count.
behaviourPage.alsoShowFilesThatChanged: Also show files that changed while an agent was working, not only its own.
behaviourPage.between1And5In: Between 1 and 5 in the morning, while an agent is idle: notes marked (until a date) go after that date, repeats are merged, and anything contradicted moves to an archive with why. Each night's changes are in that agent's Memory page, with Undo, and the morning brief mentions them.
behaviourPage.bloksSearchesTheAgentsOthe: Bloks searches the agent's other chats and notes for close matches to your message. Up to three short notes go with that message only, each saying where it came from, and your message shows what was added. Rooms and email from people you haven't listed never get them.
behaviourPage.claudeCodeCodexAndPi: Claude Code, Codex and Pi re-send the whole chat with every tool call, so one reply in a long chat can use millions of tokens. Past this size, or 60% of the model's limit, the chat is compacted before your next message. The chat marks where.
behaviourPage.claudeCodeKeepsAChat: Claude Code keeps a chat cached for an hour. The first message after that re-sends the whole chat, which costs the most. With this on, a Claude Code chat over 100k tokens that has been quiet for 55 minutes is compacted while still cached. Some detail is lost, and the chat marks where.
behaviourPage.compactLongClaudeCodeChats: Compact long Claude Code chats before their cache expires.
behaviourPage.eachRoomChoosesWhoAnswers: Each room chooses who answers in its own menu: everyone, only the lead, or Auto.
behaviourPage.forClaudeCodeCodexAnd: For Claude Code, Codex and Pi. Compact before the next message once a chat reaches this size.
behaviourPage.handFailuresToALead: Hand failures to a lead, and show you what needs you.
behaviourPage.inARoomSetTo: In a room set to Auto, a message that names nobody goes first to a small model, which picks who answers from each agent's name, role and brief and the last few messages. It has 2.5 seconds; if it runs out, is unsure or can't be reached, the lead answers. Naming someone with @ never asks it.
behaviourPage.inARoomTheRooms: In a room, the room's lead goes first. Elsewhere, this.
behaviourPage.keepEachAgentsNotesShort: Keep each agent's notes short and current while you sleep.
behaviourPage.longChatsGetSummarisedTo: Long chats get summarised to keep fitting. Off: all at once when full, with a short pause. On: a little after each reply, so no pause, but the provider can't reuse its cache, which costs more on some. Your own messages are never summarised.
behaviourPage.mostAgentRepliesInA: Most agent replies in a row
behaviourPage.mostAgentRepliesInARow: Most agent replies in a row across separate tasks
behaviourPage.nothingChangesOnItsOwn: Nothing changes on its own. New skills and changes to yours wait in Skills, with the reason, for you to keep, edit or dismiss. Each check is a call to the agent's own model, two when it changes a skill you have, on your plan or key.
behaviourPage.remindAnAgentWhatIt: Remind an agent what it said elsewhere that matches your message.
behaviourPage.sometimesACommandWaitsOn: Sometimes a command waits on something that never answers. After this long with no progress, Bloks stops the reply and tells you and the agent which call it was. Thinking, writing and commands that keep reporting are never cut short. Time waiting on your approval doesn't count.
behaviourPage.stopWhenOneCallMakes: Stop when one call makes no progress for this long.
behaviourPage.summariseALittleAfterEach: Summarise a little after each reply, not all at once.
behaviourPage.thatEngineIsNoLonger: That engine is no longer here, so Auto rooms are on their lead. Choose another.
behaviourPage.whenAReplyFailsA: When a reply fails, a tool call gets stuck, or a routine, watcher or workflow fails, whoever leads gets a quiet turn to deal with it: try it once more, pass it to a teammate, or ask you. Nothing is tried again more than once, and if many things fail in an hour you get one summary instead of a card each.
behaviourPage.whenUnsureAskTheAgents: When unsure, ask the agent's small model
behaviourPage.yourOwnMessagesAreNever: Your own messages are never summarised. Where a conversation was compacted, it says so.

cliPlugins.aProtectedTokenIsNever: A protected token is never in an agent's environment, prompt, files or output. Bloks adds it to requests to github.com and api.github.com only, and takes it back out of anything GitHub answers.
cliPlugins.addingKeysDeployKeysCollabora: Adding keys, deploy keys, collaborators, members or webhooks is never sent, whatever the grant, since each would outlast taking the grant back.
cliPlugins.agentsAreToldGhIs: Agents are told gh is signed in and to use git and gh as usual: clone, branch, push, and gh pr create. They act as this account, with its repository permissions and branch protection.
cliPlugins.anAgentCanStillMisuse: An agent can still misuse what it was granted: read access reads everything the token can, and read and write can push and open or close what the token can. Give the token only the repositories and permissions the work needs.
cliPlugins.anAgentsAddressWorksFor: An agent's address works for its own turn, for the hosts above, and only while its grant stands. Read only can clone and fetch but not push or change anything.
cliPlugins.bloksKeepsItOnThis: Bloks keeps it on this computer and adds it to agents' GitHub requests itself. No agent ever sees it.
cliPlugins.bloksKeepsNoCopyOf: Bloks keeps no copy of gh's sign-in, and it cannot keep it from an agent either: anything an agent runs, runs as you, and gh hands its token to whoever asks with gh auth token. For agents that should never hold a token, use a protected connection below.
